title: Attention Variants — Sliding Window, Sparse, Differential

questions.question: How many finite cells does causal_mask(8) contain?
questions.explanation: Row i contains i+1 allowed positions, so the lower triangle has 1+...+8 = 36 finite cells.

questions.question: For row i=7, which positions does swa_mask(8, window=4) allow?
options: Positions 0 through 7
Positions 4, 5, 6, and 7
Positions 5, 6, and 7 only
Positions 0, 3, 6, and 7
questions.explanation: The local lower bound is max(0, 7-4+1)=4, so the row attends to the four-token suffix.

questions.question: For row i=7 with window=2 and stride=3, which positions are finite in strided_mask?
options: 0 through 7
5, 6, and 7 only
1, 4, and 7 only
questions.explanation: The local window contributes 6 and 7; the strided loop contributes 0, 3, and 6, giving the union {0,3,6,7}.

questions.question: What can happen to a weight produced by diff_attention_row(..., lam=0.5)?
options: It is converted to an integer before the value sum
It must remain between 0 and 1 because both inputs are softmax rows
It is always exactly zero for the first position
It can be negative because the function subtracts 0.5*w2 from w1
questions.explanation: The differential weights are `a - lam*b`; subtracting a second attention pattern can produce negative entries even though each original row is nonnegative.

questions.question: What is the main memory benefit of a sliding window of 1,024 at N=131,072 in the demo's cache estimate?
options: It scales the full cache by 1024/131072, reducing the context-dependent portion by 128×
It removes all K/V storage and keeps only one token
It doubles the cache because every window has two directions
It changes dtype from fp16 to fp32 automatically
questions.explanation: The code sets `reduced = full * (window / N)`, and 131072/1024 = 128.

questions.question: Why does differential attention pay more KV memory in this toy comparison?
options: It stores one extra token only when a score is negative
It models two attention streams and reports `full * 2` for the sink-free weight construction
It uses no keys or values and therefore allocates a fallback tensor
It adds a classifier head with twice the vocabulary size
questions.explanation: The demo's differential row computes two attention patterns, and its cache comparison explicitly doubles the full estimate.
